violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. Observed employees touch raw meat with gloves, change gloves then touch final plates without washing hands after touching raw meat.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. CDI food discarded, hands washed, new gloves worn.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a food preparation sink, warewashing sink or in a mop sink. Observed employee wash hands in mop sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. CDI washed hands in hand sink.

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, 4 Hour Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed cutting boards , knives, tongs, spoons, salad bowls, and spatulas located at the cookline that are not being cleaned at least every 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils must be cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours to prevent contamination by bacterial growth. CDI washed and sanitized utensils

violations.title: Mechanical Warewashing, Hot Water Sanitization, 165F
violations.observation: The water temperature in the manifold servicing the high temperature warewashing machine was below the minimum allowable level of 165F for a stationary rack single temperature machine. The thermostat read 158f in the upstairs dish machine.
violations.corrective_action: In a mechanical operation the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for a stationary rack, single temperature machine or for all other machines, 180F. CDI down stairs dish machine will be used.

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Process
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not properly cooked using a non-continuous cooking process: lamb chops and beef skewers without a written procedure approved by the health department. Observed meats sitting on table shelf waiting to be fully cooked. Observed at 85f
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be subject to an initial heating process that is no longer than 60 minutes in duration; immediately, after initial heating, cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified for cooked time/temperature control for safety food; after cooling, held frozenor cold; prior to sale or service, cooked using a process that heats all parts of the food to a temperature and for a time as specified under 3-401.11A-C; Cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified under 3-501.14A if not hot held, served immediately or held using time as a public health control. CDI meat fully cooked. Establishment will cease partial cooking until submission and approval of procedures. Submit written procedure to the health department for approval.

violations.title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods, Minimum of 165F
violations.observation: The following poultry item was not cooked to a sufficient temperature and/or time to eliminate pathogenic bacteria: chicken breast 164f
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods such as poultry, wild game animals, stuffed fish, stuffed meat, stuffed pasta, stuffed poultry, stuffed ratites, or stuffing containing any of these raw animal foods shall be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165F for at least 15 seconds. CDI cooked to 165f for 15s

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. Steamed corn 72f after 3 hours
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. CDI discarded

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Observed beef drippings, mushrooms, and pasta over 41f after cooling 6 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. CDI discarded

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: mashed potatoes 114f in warmer
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI reheated to 165f in microwave

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: tomatoes, marinated tomatoes, corn, cheese, compound butter, garlic oil, milk, calamari , lettuce, chicken burritos, chicken, chicken tender batter, and honey butter
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI discarded food

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC (4 Hour), Initial Temp of 41F or 135F
violations.observation: Observed mashed potatoes (111f) on steam well placed on time control without reaching 135f initial temperature after not being properly hot held in warming cabinet prior.
violations.corrective_action: A hot food using time control for safety must start the 4 hour time at a temperature 135f or above. CDI mashed potatoes reheated to 165f.

violations.title: TPHC, Food Cannot Exceed 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is being used as a control was not cooked, served or discarded by the expiration time as indicated: garlic oil/ compound butter/ farro salad/ salsa not discarded after 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours is used as the public health control : 1) the food shall have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature or, 2) the food shall have an initial temperature of 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 3) the food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 4) the food shall be cooked and served, served if ready to eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 5) the food if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit shall be discarded. CDI discarded MIKE'S AMERICAN GRILL (Inspection Date: 09/04/2026) Page 3 of 5

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): garlic oil/ compound butter/ farro salad/ salsa/ and mashed potatoes.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. CDI written procedure provided. Time written on each food item

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: garlic oil/ compound butter/ farro salad/ and salsa not marked.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI marked with 4 hour time

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed large deep plastic containers being used to cool food.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI DISCUSSED COOLING METHODS AND PROVIDED HANDOUTS. DO NOT UES DEEP PLASTIC CONTAINER FOR COOLING, THOSE ARE ONLY USE FOR STORAGE.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squirt bottles with lemon oil, olive sauce, and oils.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CDI labeled

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: cold wells downstairs, chicken tender prep cooler upstairs.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Items kept on time control for 4 hours. Have coolers fixed

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: dish machine upstairs.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Do not use for sanitizing until repaired

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Thermometer for Manual Wash & Sanitizing Temps
violations.observation: No thermometer available for testing temperature of water used for sanitization. Observed battery dead and thermometer inoperable. PIC not checking internal dish machine temperature for sanitizing.
violations.corrective_action: In manual warewashing operations, a temperature measuring device shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and sanitizing temperatures. CDI new thermometer borrowed from another store. Replace batteries in original thermometer.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: multiple raw food items were being stored next to one another in the 3DR UCR in the first floor kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT PROPER STORAGE OF RAW AND READY TO EAT FOOD ITEMS. PIC MOVED ALL RAW FOODS OUT OF COOLER, TO ONLY LEAVE THE RTE FOOD ITEMS.

violations.title: Mechanical Warewashing, Hot Water Sanitization, 165F
violations.observation: The water temperature in the manifold servicing the high temperature warewashing machine was below the minimum allowable level of 165F for a stationary rack single temperature machine. The minimum temperature for the High Temp Dish Machine in the 2nd floor kitchen needed to reach a minimum temp of 165F, while the actual temperature was 154F.
violations.corrective_action: In a mechanical operation the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for a stationary rack, single temperature machine or for all other machines, 180F. PIC KNEW THE DISH WASHER WAS AN ISSUE BEFORE INSPECTION AND HAD A PLUMBER ON SITE TO FIX THE HOT WATER DURING THE INSPECTION. THE PLUMBER WAS ABLE TO GET THE WATER TO THE PROPER TEMPERATURE FOR SANITIZATION.
